value.title: Torvald Klaveness
value.description: Klaveness is a pioneering, data-driven, and safety-oriented shipping company with a vision to improve the nature of shipping.
value.main_text_excerpt:
OUR VISION
Torvald Klaveness has challenged the status quo for almost 80 years. The success and legacy of the company is anchored in finding new ways to improve technology and business models in shipping.
Our vision of improving the nature of shipping underpins the work we do and our continuous commitment to change and improve the industry we are a part of.
OUR BUSINESSES
Klaveness Combination Carriers ASA
Torvald Klaveness is the main shareholder of Klaveness Combination Carriers ASA, a company listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange (ticker: “KCC”).
The fleet of 19 combination carriers mainly operate in optimized trade patterns, switching between dry and wet cargoes with minimum ballast. As a result, the fleet delivers up to 40% lower greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional dry bulk and tanker vessels performing the same transport work.
Klaveness Digital
Klaveness Digital AS, a company fully owned by Torvald Klaveness, is responsible for the innovation process, and the development and commercialization of digital services across the Klaveness Group.
They deliver real-time insights that help companies navigate complexity, reduce risk, and improve efficiency across their supply chains and commercial operations.
Klaveness Dry Bulk
Klaveness Dry Bulk, 75% owned by Torvald Klaveness, is a leading operator in the global dry bulk industry and manages the world’s largest Panamax Pool. 
They enable customers and partners to navigate market volatility, optimize performance, and create lasting value by combining innovative business models, strategic partnerships, and digital solutions.

pages.title: About Us — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
ABOUT US
Klaveness is a pioneering shipping company that delivers a portfolio of physical and digital services to the maritime industry.
80 YEARS OF INNOVATION
VISION AND VALUES
At the core of Torvald Klaveness are the values we live by and the vision we pursue. Our vision is to improve the nature of shipping.
Our legacy is to challenge status quo, and much of our success has been, and is linked to, finding new ways to improve technology and business models in shipping.
The vision provides direction and guiding along three dimensions:
IMPROVING
We always look for new solutions
THE NATURE
Our ambition is to improve the very nature of the business we are in
OF SHIPPING
Shipping is our market and where we can make a difference
Our values define what we stand for and what you can expect from us:
Craftsmanship
We know our business in detail:
- Constantly update and renew competence
- Deliver as promised
- Build and contribute to teams
- Keep it simple
Integrity
We act on our principles:
- Ethics before profits
- Be honest
- Express your concerns
- Address problems
Commitment
We see through cycles:
- Seek lasting solutions
- Never bet the company
- Support the customer
- Never give up
Curiosity
We challenge established thinking:
- Ask questions
- Look for new solutions
- Share with and build on insights of others
- Try a little, learn a lot

pages.title: Governance — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
GOVERNANCE
Klaveness believes transparent and good corporate governance drives value creation by aligning stakeholder and company interests
The main governance structure and principles are as follows:
- Trond Harald Klaveness is the sole owner and Chair of the Board of Rederiaksjeselskapet Torvald Klaveness (RASTK). The RASTK Board of Directors further comprises independent representatives with extensive corporate experience, Christian Rynning-Tønnesen, Rebekka Glasser Herlofsen, Elisabeth Tørstad, and Mehrdad Amini.
- Ernst Meyer is the President and CEO of Torvald Klaveness and heads up Klaveness Holding and the Klaveness Executive Committee.
- Torvald Klaveness has incorporated a holding structure with a top management team responsible for developing and implementing corporate strategy, execute active ownership of the existing portfolio of companies, drive new strategic investments, and actively manage a portfolio of liquid financial investments.
- The Group's portfolio companies include Klaveness Digital (100% owned), Klaveness Dry Bulk (75% owned by Klaveness and 25% owned by Marubeni Corporation), and Klaveness Combination Carriers (KCC), in which Klaveness holds approximately 44% of the shares. KCC is listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
- KCC and KDB are governed through separate Boards of Directors, these consist of board representatives from the Holding team and external directors.
- Company headquarters are Oslo, Norway, with subsidiaries operating in Singapore, Japan, Manila, and Dubai.
- Safety, Risk Management, Compliance, Cyber-security, Human Rights and ESG in general are integral parts of our business. We have dedicated people, functions, policies, governance, and management attention in place to execute safe and responsible business practices. Our compliance program is mandatory for all employees, officers, and directors.
- We operate under a Code of Conduct that is accepted in writing by each employee, officer, and director.

pages.title: Working with us — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
CAREERS
Keen to make a difference?
Join us on a journey to improve the nature of shipping
What we are looking for
We seek to attract and retain the best people and make sure they can reach their full potential.
We believe in, and encourage, long term professional and personal growth. We strive to build strong communities where people commit themselves, challenge each other, and where we develop together.
A team member of Klaveness is passionate, up for challenges, and willing to explore the boundaries of their own comfort zone. We believe this is key in today’s knowledge economy and fundamental in our commitment to challenge the status quo and bring new opportunities to deep-sea shipping.
Klaveness Academy
Equipping our employees with the right skills and tools, at the right time is essential. We value growth and foster a culture of learning and development that encourage our pioneers to become the best versions of themselves.
To meet this need, we have developed our very own educational hub - Klaveness Academy. We believe in lifelong learning and the Academy offers just that through three main programs:
- Decarbonization by Klaveness Academy
- The Klaveness Analytics program
- The Klaveness Compliance program
We are always looking for talented people who are driven by success, innovation, and self-development to join our team. We value diversity and depend on a wide spectrum of competence across the business to fulfil our everyday needs.
As a member of the Klaveness team, you will be passionate about creating sustainable solutions for our own operations as well as those of our customers. You will apply cutting edge technology and digital solutions to employ data driven decisions in all areas of our business. You will contribute to decarbonizing global shipping and play a key role in one of the biggest challenges of this generation.
Starting your journey with Klaveness today will see you join an ambition to make seaborne supply chains, resilient, decarbonized, and cost-effective.

pages.title: Klaveness Dry Bulk completes milestone clinker shipment — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Klaveness Dry Bulk completes milestone clinker shipment
In August 2026, Klaveness Dry Bulk completed its first cement clinker shipment in several years, loading in Cam Pha, Vietnam, and discharging in Ivory Coast, Africa. The voyage marked a milestone in a trade that is evolving alongside changing supply chains and port infrastructure.
Traditionally, clinker imports to West Africa have been carried on geared vessels. However, changing market conditions and reduced steel production in Europe has shifted sourcing patterns, with clinker increasingly sourced from Vietnam and South China and transported on larger, gearless Panamax vessels. At scale, these vessels can benefit from trading positions closer to the vibrant East Coast South America grain markets, in turn helping eliminate ballast voyages.
At the same time, significant investments in port infrastructure across West Africa have expanded opportunities for these larger vessels. While we, together with the various stakeholders involved in the voyage, continue to face the challenges of port congestion, we see this as an interesting and evolving trade pattern.
At Klaveness Dry Bulk and Baumarine, we will continue to support this trade and be a committed partner, helping move cargo efficiently between Asia and West Africa while supporting industrial growth and infrastructure development in the region.

pages.title: Reflections on trading efficiency after a visit to M/V Penta — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Reflections on trading efficiency after a visit to M/V Penta
This summer, the Klaveness Japan team were joined by Ryo Miura, Japanese representative of Baumarine by Klaveness pool member Taiship, for a visit to M/V Penta while the vessel was discharging grain in Mizushima, Japan. Beyond providing a close-up view of operations, the visit gave our team the opportunity to reflect on how strong collaboration can unlock greater trading efficiency in practice.
Recently redelivered from a previous charter and approaching its 15-year special survey, Penta impressed the team with its condition and operational readiness. Haruki Chua, General Manager of Klaveness Japan, commented that while some charterers may become more selective as vessels age, Penta demonstrated how the right vessel can continue to create clear value when matched with the right trade. "With a bit of craftsmanship, we were able to identify a trade where Penta could load almost as much as a Kamsarmax in the draft restricted ports of Japan."
Haruki also noted that the voyage highlighted how trading efficiency often extends well beyond the performance of a single vessel. Originally planned as a two-port discharge across opposite ends of Japan, the voyage took an unexpected turn when a stockout at a neighboring silo in Mizushima created an opportunity for different receivers to swap cargoes between vessels. The adjustment enabled all receivers to receive their cargo on time, while improving vessel positioning for the next trades.
For Penta, the change meant saving two and a half days of ballast towards her dry dock. For the other vessel involved, it reduced unnecessary sailing time and left it better positioned for its next North Pacific employment. Together, the result was improved utilization and a more efficient outcome for all parties.
For Junji Aratani, Chartering Manager in Japan, the experience reinforced the bigger picture on the value that can be created through closer collaboration: "While this efficiency gain was triggered by an unexpected cargo shortage, it highlighted what is possible when owners and charterers work together at a deeper level. Lower average freight costs, reduced emissions, and a more efficient fleet are just the tip of the iceberg."

pages.title: Torvald Klaveness 2006–2016: Charting a new course — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Torvald Klaveness 2006–2016: Charting a new course
Part 7 of an 8-part story through the decades to mark our 80th anniversary
By the mid-2000s, Klaveness had expanded its international presence, continued developing new shipping activities, and built interests that extended well beyond traditional ship ownership.
Over the next ten years, the company’s structure, leadership and strategic direction would change significantly. As markets evolved and the business developed, Klaveness increasingly sharpened its focus around shipping and related maritime activities.
A vision to ‘improve the nature of shipping’
The decade saw Klaveness continue reshaping its broad portfolio of activities. A significant step came with the sale of the transloader business, which generated substantial gain for the company.
Later in the decade, a defining moment came in 2011 when the wider Klaveness group was divided into two separate businesses. Investment activities in real estate and financial markets were separated from the core shipping operations, giving the shipping company strategic focus on developing its maritime activities.
The restructuring coincided with a major leadership transition. In 2011, Lasse Kristoffersen became the first CEO in the company’s history from outside the Klaveness family. Under this new era of leadership, Klaveness developed the vision and values that continue to guide the company today.
Strengthening the shipping platform
While these changes were taking place, Klaveness continued developing its dry bulk activities and strengthening its presence in Asia. Klaveness Asia Pte. Ltd. was established in Singapore in 2006, strengthening the company’s commercial presence in a region of growing importance to global shipping.
The combination carrier business also continued to evolve. Another first-generation CABU joined the fleet in 2007, while the first vessels in a larger second generation entered service at the end of the decade. These ‘CABU II’ vessels offered increased cargo capacity while continuing to serve the caustic soda and dry bulk trading patterns established by the original CABUs.
Work also began on extending the combination carrier concept into new cargo markets. This laid the groundwork for the CLEANBU vessels, which would enter service in the following decade and carry clean petroleum products as well as dry bulk cargoes.
Investing in people
Klaveness’ development depended not only on vessels and markets, but also on the people supporting its operations, both at sea and onshore.
During the decade, the company strengthened its approach to employee development through a more structured performance and development process, greater emphasis on leadership development and internal training in areas including safety and compliance.
At sea, Klaveness had longstanding crewing activities in the Philippines, supported by cadetship and manpower development programs designed to recruit, train and develop seafarers over the long term.
During the decade, South Africa also began emerging as a new source of maritime talent. The initiative built on the company’s established approach to recruitment, training and development and expanded its global crewing capabilities.
The digital era
Toward the end of the decade, a new strategic direction placed greater emphasis on innovation and digital capability. ‘KLAB’ was established in 2015 as a pilot initiative to explore how technology and data could improve the way Klaveness worked, interacted with customers and operated its vessels.
KLAB quickly moved beyond the pilot phase, with several digital solutions already in regular use by the end of the period. The initiative helped lay the foundation for the digital business and customer-facing commercial solutions that emerged in the following decade.
As these ten years drew to a close, Klaveness had sharpened its focus around shipping while continuing to develop its fleet, global presence, and maritime expertise. A new generation of combination carriers was entering service, work on future digital products was underway, and the company had begun building capabilities that would shape its next chapter.

- Next | Torvald Klaveness 2016–2026

Keen to make a difference?
Join us on a journey to improve the nature of shipping
What we are looking for
We seek to attract and retain the best people and make sure they can reach their full potential.
We believe in, and encourage, long term professional and personal growth. We strive to build strong communities where people commit themselves, challenge each other, and where we develop together.
A team member of Klaveness is passionate, up for challenges, and willing to explore the boundaries of their own comfort zone. We believe this is key in today’s knowledge economy and fundamental in our commitment to challenge the status quo and bring new opportunities to deep-sea shipping.
Klaveness Academy
Equipping our employees with the right skills and tools, at the right time is essential. We value growth and foster a culture of learning and development that encourage our pioneers to become the best versions of themselves.
To meet this need, we have developed our very own educational hub - Klaveness Academy. We believe in lifelong learning and the Academy offers just that through three main programs:
- Decarbonization by Klaveness Academy
- The Klaveness Analytics program
- The Klaveness Compliance program
We are always looking for talented people who are driven by success, innovation, and self-development to join our team. We value diversity and depend on a wide spectrum of competence across the business to fulfil our everyday needs.
As a member of the Klaveness team, you will be passionate about creating sustainable solutions for our own operations as well as those of our customers. You will apply cutting edge technology and digital solutions to employ data driven decisions in all areas of our business. You will contribute to decarbonizing global shipping and play a key role in one of the biggest challenges of this generation.
Starting your journey with Klaveness today will see you join an ambition to make seaborne supply chains, resilient, decarbonized, and cost-effective.

pages.title: Klaveness Dry Bulk completes milestone clinker shipment — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Klaveness Dry Bulk completes milestone clinker shipment
In August 2026, Klaveness Dry Bulk completed its first cement clinker shipment in several years, loading in Cam Pha, Vietnam, and discharging in Ivory Coast, Africa. The voyage marked a milestone in a trade that is evolving alongside changing supply chains and port infrastructure.
Traditionally, clinker imports to West Africa have been carried on geared vessels. However, changing market conditions and reduced steel production in Europe has shifted sourcing patterns, with clinker increasingly sourced from Vietnam and South China and transported on larger, gearless Panamax vessels. At scale, these vessels can benefit from trading positions closer to the vibrant East Coast South America grain markets, in turn helping eliminate ballast voyages.
At the same time, significant investments in port infrastructure across West Africa have expanded opportunities for these larger vessels. While we, together with the various stakeholders involved in the voyage, continue to face the challenges of port congestion, we see this as an interesting and evolving trade pattern.
At Klaveness Dry Bulk and Baumarine, we will continue to support this trade and be a committed partner, helping move cargo efficiently between Asia and West Africa while supporting industrial growth and infrastructure development in the region.

pages.title: Reflections on trading efficiency after a visit to M/V Penta — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Reflections on trading efficiency after a visit to M/V Penta
This summer, the Klaveness Japan team were joined by Ryo Miura, Japanese representative of Baumarine by Klaveness pool member Taiship, for a visit to M/V Penta while the vessel was discharging grain in Mizushima, Japan. Beyond providing a close-up view of operations, the visit gave our team the opportunity to reflect on how strong collaboration can unlock greater trading efficiency in practice.
Recently redelivered from a previous charter and approaching its 15-year special survey, Penta impressed the team with its condition and operational readiness. Haruki Chua, General Manager of Klaveness Japan, commented that while some charterers may become more selective as vessels age, Penta demonstrated how the right vessel can continue to create clear value when matched with the right trade. "With a bit of craftsmanship, we were able to identify a trade where Penta could load almost as much as a Kamsarmax in the draft restricted ports of Japan."
Haruki also noted that the voyage highlighted how trading efficiency often extends well beyond the performance of a single vessel. Originally planned as a two-port discharge across opposite ends of Japan, the voyage took an unexpected turn when a stockout at a neighboring silo in Mizushima created an opportunity for different receivers to swap cargoes between vessels. The adjustment enabled all receivers to receive their cargo on time, while improving vessel positioning for the next trades.
For Penta, the change meant saving two and a half days of ballast towards her dry dock. For the other vessel involved, it reduced unnecessary sailing time and left it better positioned for its next North Pacific employment. Together, the result was improved utilization and a more efficient outcome for all parties.
For Junji Aratani, Chartering Manager in Japan, the experience reinforced the bigger picture on the value that can be created through closer collaboration: "While this efficiency gain was triggered by an unexpected cargo shortage, it highlighted what is possible when owners and charterers work together at a deeper level. Lower average freight costs, reduced emissions, and a more efficient fleet are just the tip of the iceberg."

pages.title: Torvald Klaveness 2006–2016: Charting a new course — Torvald Klaveness
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Torvald Klaveness 2006–2016: Charting a new course
Part 7 of an 8-part story through the decades to mark our 80th anniversary
By the mid-2000s, Klaveness had expanded its international presence, continued developing new shipping activities, and built interests that extended well beyond traditional ship ownership.
Over the next ten years, the company’s structure, leadership and strategic direction would change significantly. As markets evolved and the business developed, Klaveness increasingly sharpened its focus around shipping and related maritime activities.
A vision to ‘improve the nature of shipping’
The decade saw Klaveness continue reshaping its broad portfolio of activities. A significant step came with the sale of the transloader business, which generated substantial gain for the company.
Later in the decade, a defining moment came in 2011 when the wider Klaveness group was divided into two separate businesses. Investment activities in real estate and financial markets were separated from the core shipping operations, giving the shipping company strategic focus on developing its maritime activities.
The restructuring coincided with a major leadership transition. In 2011, Lasse Kristoffersen became the first CEO in the company’s history from outside the Klaveness family. Under this new era of leadership, Klaveness developed the vision and values that continue to guide the company today.
Strengthening the shipping platform
While these changes were taking place, Klaveness continued developing its dry bulk activities and strengthening its presence in Asia. Klaveness Asia Pte. Ltd. was established in Singapore in 2006, strengthening the company’s commercial presence in a region of growing importance to global shipping.
The combination carrier business also continued to evolve. Another first-generation CABU joined the fleet in 2007, while the first vessels in a larger second generation entered service at the end of the decade. These ‘CABU II’ vessels offered increased cargo capacity while continuing to serve the caustic soda and dry bulk trading patterns established by the original CABUs.
Work also began on extending the combination carrier concept into new cargo markets. This laid the groundwork for the CLEANBU vessels, which would enter service in the following decade and carry clean petroleum products as well as dry bulk cargoes.
Investing in people
Klaveness’ development depended not only on vessels and markets, but also on the people supporting its operations, both at sea and onshore.
During the decade, the company strengthened its approach to employee development through a more structured performance and development process, greater emphasis on leadership development and internal training in areas including safety and compliance.
At sea, Klaveness had longstanding crewing activities in the Philippines, supported by cadetship and manpower development programs designed to recruit, train and develop seafarers over the long term.
During the decade, South Africa also began emerging as a new source of maritime talent. The initiative built on the company’s established approach to recruitment, training and development and expanded its global crewing capabilities.
The digital era
Toward the end of the decade, a new strategic direction placed greater emphasis on innovation and digital capability. ‘KLAB’ was established in 2015 as a pilot initiative to explore how technology and data could improve the way Klaveness worked, interacted with customers and operated its vessels.
KLAB quickly moved beyond the pilot phase, with several digital solutions already in regular use by the end of the period. The initiative helped lay the foundation for the digital business and customer-facing commercial solutions that emerged in the following decade.
As these ten years drew to a close, Klaveness had sharpened its focus around shipping while continuing to develop its fleet, global presence, and maritime expertise. A new generation of combination carriers was entering service, work on future digital products was underway, and the company had begun building capabilities that would shape its next chapter.
